ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based PEP screening aligned with FINTRAC guidance under PCMLTFA; mandatory screening against Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions lists (Special Economic Measures Act, United Nations Act, Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act), OFAC SDN list (required for USD rails via Wise/SWIFT), UN Security Council sanctions, and UK/EU lists where counterparties require; enhanced due diligence for non-resident UBOs and source-of-wealth verification for any politically exposed person; ongoing transactional monitoring and quarterly reverification; records retained five years per FINTRAC requirements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Alberta Corporate Access, Service Alberta); NUANS name search report must be obtained through an authorized Registry Agent before filing Articles of Incorporation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must use Latin alphabetic characters in English or French; non-Latin script UBO and corporate names must be transliterated into English/French; the legal element 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or the abbreviation 'ULC' must appear as the designated suffix (French equivalent permitted where applicable); numerical names are permitted but remain subject to NUANS conflict review.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Trust, Loan, Insurance, Assurance (regulated financial services, prior consent of applicable regulator required)
University, College, Institute (regulated post-secondary terms, prior ministerial approval required)
Engineer, Engineering, Architecture (professional designation protected under Alberta statutes)
Barrister, Solicitor, Attorney, Law (law society restricted terms)
Medical, Physician, Clinic, Pharmacy, Ambulance (health-regulated terms)
Royal, Imperial, Crown (federal/provincial Crown consent required)
Canada, Canadian, Government, Municipal (government marker restrictions)
Co-operative, Condominium, Society (governed by specific Alberta statutes)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within the 90-day NUANS validity window, counsel may refile with a revised name and a fresh NUANS report; upon rejection, the applicant may submit a written administrative appeal to the Alberta Corporate Registry through a licensed Registry Agent, attaching a legal rationale with trademark registry evidence, NUANS search analysis, and supporting case authority; if the Registrar maintains the refusal, final recourse is an application for judicial review to the Alberta Court of King's Bench within the applicable limitation period.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted: the Alberta Business Corporations Act requires a physical address in Alberta (not a PO Box) for service of process and maintenance of records; a licensed commercial registered-agent virtual office satisfies this requirement and is accepted for the 3D animation/VFX industry, as no physical production premises or storefront in Alberta is mandated for ISIC 5911 activities; books and records may be kept at the registered office or at another location in Alberta as directed by the directors.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: estimated annual probability of a physical unannounced on-site inspection is below 10% for a low-risk digital-services ULC; inspection triggers would include CRA tax audit, Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration verification, FINTRAC examination at the financial-institution level, or an integrity check during banking onboarding; no sector-specific licensing inspections apply to ISIC 5911 commercial animation production.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended; ss. 15.1 et seq. (unlimited liability corporations), s. 101 (articles of incorporation), s. 102 (use of name with ULC descriptor), ss. 106, 202–211 (directors, officers and records); and the Alberta Business Corporations Regulations, Alta Reg 190/2020.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction (Registrar of Corporations)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation filed together with Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors under the Alberta Business Corporations Act; issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation completes statutory formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital and no escrow capital requirement under the ABCA for an Alberta ULC. The articles must authorize at least one class of unlimited-liability shares; shares may be issued for consideration fixed by the board, including cash, property or past services, and the consideration must be recorded in the share register.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
BE IT RESOLVED:
1. That the Corporation subscribes for and accepts the allotment of unlimited-liability shares set out in the articles, at the consideration fixed by the board, and that certificates be issued accordingly.
2. That the registered office be located at the address identified in the Notice of Registered Office, and the corporate records be maintained there.
3. That the following officers be appointed: President, Secretary-Treasurer, and such other officers as the board may approve, each to serve until successor selection.
4. That the board adopt incorporation-related by-laws and ratify all pre-incorporation contracts.
5. That officers are authorized to execute and deliver all ancillary filings and banking resolutions necessary to give effect to this resolution.
All previous resolutions are confirmed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and NUANS Corporate Name Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction) through an accredited NUANS service provider or Registry Connect
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS preliminary name search; select an available corporate name ending with 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC' as required for an Alberta ULC; assess distinctiveness under the ABCA name rules; reserve the name online and retain the NUANS report for filing.
required_dossiers: Proposed Articles of Incorporation name draft
Consent to use of a name or distinctive element, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit a revised NUANS search with a more distinctive element or file a request for reconsideration with the Registrar; registry staff will indicate whether a formal appeal is necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Filing of Articles of Incorporation and Statutory First Notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction (Registrar of Corporations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Articles of Incorporation providing ULC status, authorized share structure, registered office address, first directors and any unanimous shareholder agreement; execute and submit the Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors; file online through Registry Connect or deliver in person to the Registrar; pay the applicable state fee.
required_dossiers: Authorization for share issuance and ULC designation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues an objection or requisition, file Amended Articles or a Notice of Correction within the prescribed response window; correct signature or address defects and resubmit to the same Registry file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and ULC Endorsement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After statutory review, the Registrar endorses the Articles and issues the Certificate of Incorporation; verify the corporate name, Alberta jurisdiction and ULC designation; confirm the incorporation date and registered office in the profile.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request a certificate correction or reissuance through Service Alberta if the certificate contains a clerical error; provide supporting corporate records and pay the correction fee if applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitution of First Board, Share Subscription and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation itself, acting through the incorporator and first directors; no separate government filing is required for ordinary officer appointments in Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold a preliminary meeting or pass unanimous written resolutions as first board; approve the share subscription and allotment, issue share certificates, adopt by-laws, appoint officers, open the corporate minute book and share register, and confirm the registered office authority.
required_dossiers: First board meeting minutes or written resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a share allotment is challenged, the board may rescind or reissue affected shares by supplemental board resolution; ensure unlimited liability disclosure and ABCA solvency conditions are satisfied before issuing further shares.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax Registration and Business Number Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Registration Online), with Alberta corporate tax administered under the Alberta Tax Administration Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the newly incorporated ULC with the CRA for a federal Business Number and applicable program accounts, including GST/HST, payroll deductions, and Alberta corporate income tax where required; provide the corporate name, incorporation date, registered office and responsible officer information.
required_dossiers: Expected annual GST/HST taxable supplies declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries the application, submit a letter of explanation with the Certificate of Incorporation and Notice of Directors; CRA may assign the Business Number back to the date of incorporation, retroactive to the registration date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Premises Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal business licensing department of the city or town where the commercial CGI/3D animation studio is operated (e.g., Calgary Licensing Department or Edmonton Business Licensing Centre)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a municipal business licence and occupancy permit for the commercial office or studio premises; supply a lease or proof of ownership, zoning confirmation for commercial/office use, and evidence of fire safety and building code compliance before commencing animation production activities.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or certificate of title
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If licensing or zoning is refused, apply for a discretionary development approval or variance under the applicable municipal land-use bylaw or relocate the studio to a properly zoned commercial or industrial premise; appeal an adverse decision through the municipal subdivision and development appeal board.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No dedicated federal or provincial statutory licensing board applies to ISIC 5911 / NAICS 512110 commercial CGI and 3D animation production; the competent authorities are the municipal licensing department for business and occupancy, and Alberta Environment and Protected Areas for environmental matters at the physical studio premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business and Occupancy Licence issued under the Municipal Government Act, RSA 2000, c M-26 and local business-licensing bylaw; no federal or provincial production licence is required for the animation business activity itself.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-12
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no full EIA report required. A digital animation/VFX studio is a low-impact commercial office occupancy that does not trigger a mandatory EIA registration or baseline study; municipal development approval may apply routine environmental screening for site servicing.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater and minimal VOC/PM emissions are anticipated from computer-based animation and rendering workstations. If emergency generators, spray booths or industrial HVAC are installed, comply with the Alberta Ambient Air Quality Objectives and applicable Code of Practice. Electronic waste and batteries must be handled through approved e-waste channels under the Waste Control Regulation, Alta Reg 192/1996, and domestic sewage discharges must comply with municipal sanitary sewer bylaws.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the local fire authority under the Alberta Fire Code; building occupancy permit confirming structural floor load, means of egress and life safety under the Alberta Building Code; workplace health and safety clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act, RSA 2000, c O-2.1 and the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada — federal corporate tax (Income Tax Act) and GST/HST (Excise Tax Act). Alberta corporate income tax (Alberta Corporate Tax Act) is collected by the CRA under the Canada-Alberta Federal-Provincial Tax Collection Agreement. Portals: Business Registration Online, CRA My Business Account, GST/HST NETFILE (canada.ca/en/revenue-agency).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The Alberta ULC is first incorporated through the Alberta Corporate Registry, obtaining a Corporate Access Number. The CRA then assigns the 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) with program accounts: RT (corporate income tax), RC (GST/HST), RP (payroll). Incorporations effected electronically through the Alberta registry are auto-registered with CRA via Business Registration Online; foreign-owned or non-resident ULCs must confirm registration by filing Form RC1 and may require CRA non-resident business registration (Form RC4312) and an Alberta corporate tax (AT) program account. The RC (GST/HST) account must be in place once taxable supplies made in Canada exceed CAD 30,000; foreign-owned ULCs must also report under Form T2104/T2147 where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — For Canadian domestic tax purposes the Alberta ULC is an entity-level taxed taxable Canadian corporation (federal Part I general rate 15%; Alberta general corporate rate 8%); no federal or Alberta capital tax applies. For U.S. federal tax purposes the ULC is not a per se corporation under Treas. Reg. § 301.7701-2(b)(8) and may be classified as a disregarded entity or partnership, producing a deliberate hybrid: Canadian entity-level taxation with U.S. flow-through treatment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No domestic check-the-box election exists: the ULC is a corporation under the Income Tax Act. U.S. shareholders elect under Form 8832 (check-the-box) for disregarded-entity or partnership classification. The Canada-U.S. Tax Treaty (5th Protocol, Art. IV(6)) fiscally transparent entity rule governs treaty eligibility for income flowing through the ULC; dividends paid by the ULC attract Part XIII withholding (treaty rate 5% with substantive shareholding / 15% otherwise), while an 8832 election may shift character to U.S. shareholders. Alberta uniquely permits a 100%-owned affiliated group to file a consolidated Alberta corporate return; no federal consolidated filing exists — federal group relief is limited to loss-transfer funding under ITA s. 111(1)(d).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) / Harmonized Sales Tax (HST). Alberta is a non-participating province with no provincial sales tax; only the federal 5% GST applies to taxable supplies made in Alberta.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — 'small supplier' threshold (ETA s. 148(1)): GST/HST registration is mandatory once taxable supplies made in Canada (including zero-rated export services) exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or over four consecutive calendar quarters. Registration, once triggered, applies from the supply; voluntary registration is permitted to claim input tax credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory clearance API exists in Canada (unlike LATAM/EU clearance regimes). Statutory invoice content requires the supplier's BN/RC account number, date, description, tax status, and GST amount (ETA ss. 223–224.1; GST/HST Memorandum 10.4). Electronic remittance (GST/HST NETFILE) is mandatory for all corporations and registrants above CAD 1.5M in taxable supplies. The CRA is adopting voluntary PEPPOL BIS 3.0 e-invoicing for federal procurement; B2B commercial e-invoicing is not legally mandated.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of CGI/VFX/3D animation services is zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7 where supplied to a non-resident and not rendered to an individual in Canada nor in respect of real property in Canada; licensing of animation copyrights to non-residents is zero-rated under s. 10 (intangible personal property for use outside Canada). Physical deliverables (masters, media) are zero-rated under s. 9. Substantiation requires proof of non-resident recipient, use wholly outside Canada, and arm's-length commercial terms; services physically performed in Canada for a Canadian-based production entity remain taxable at 5%. The ETA imposes no statutory FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day intercompany cash-conversion benchmark is the administrative standard applied by CRA in transfer-pricing (ITA s. 247) audits.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A) filed with CBSA for physical goods or valuable media exceeding CAD 2,000; pure digital FTP/cloud deliverables require a service export commercial invoice instead
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill proving physical delivery of masters or deliverables to the non-resident customer
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 / Wise B2B statement evidencing foreign-currency settlement from the non-resident payor
Executed service or licence agreement stating supply to a non-resident for use wholly outside Canada, together with CRA Information Circular IC 7-5 non-residency evidence pack
GST/HST export documentation and input-tax-credit support file (Form GST66 rebate route where applicable)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA applies the four-year normal reassessment window (ETA s. 298; extended to seven years where misrepresentation or negligence is shown). Deficient export substantiation triggers reassessment at 5% GST with daily compound prescribed interest, late-filing and remittance penalties under ETA s. 280 (1% of unremitted tax plus 0.25% per month, capped at 4%), and a 50% gross-negligence penalty under s. 285.1; s. 327 permits fines up to 200% of evaded tax plus imprisonment. ITCs embedded in export costs are retrospectively clawed back where the 'use wholly outside Canada' test fails. Related-party service exports are concurrently audited under ITA s. 247 transfer-pricing rules requiring contemporaneous Form T106 documentation; adjustments carry a 10% penalty plus interest and reassessment of the 180-day repatriation benchmark. VFX and digital services supplied to foreign studios are a specific CRA audit flag where the Canadian recipient is a disregarded subsidiary.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains free convertibility for current account transactions in compliance with IMF Article VIII. Capital account transactions are subject to review by the Bank of Canada and OSFI for national security and anti-money laundering purposes. Profit remittances to non-resident shareholders are generally permitted without prior approval for routine corporate distributions, subject only to tax withholding at source and beneficial ownership verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory requirement for surrender of export proceeds. Canadian companies may retain foreign currency earnings offshore or repatriate at market rates. All export receipts must be fully documented for accounting, tax filing, and AML purposes with no mandatory conversion ratios or surrender timelines imposed by the Bank of Canada.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Limited feasibility for offshore digital EMIs. Canadian entities must comply with OSFI and FINTRAC oversight. Platforms such as Wise Business support corporate cross-border transfers but do not confer full EMI status and remain subject to licensing, AML, and payment services regulations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote corporate account opening is permitted for Alberta ULCs provided incorporation documents are verified. Directors and signatories must complete video KYC interviews and submit original identification documents, particularly for transactions exceeding internal thresholds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value inbound capital injections from foreign sources
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source of funds evidence, beneficial ownership declaration, corporate board resolution, and arm's-length investment confirmation

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions involving politically exposed persons or high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence reports, senior management approval, and continuous transaction monitoring records

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injections via SWIFT MT103 wires from foreign parents or investors. Use purpose codes such as 'EQ' for equity contributions or 'LOAN' for intercompany loans. All wires require full beneficiary details, payment purpose, and supporting documentation for Canadian bank AML verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements employ SWIFT MT103 for international transfers or issuance of Commercial Letters of Credit through correspondent banks. Animation production disbursements to suppliers or freelancers are routed via MT103 using purpose codes such as 'SERV' for services rendered.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the corporation's anniversary date of incorporation each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty applies under Alberta corporate registry schedule; failure to file for two consecutive years may subject the Alberta Unlimited Liability Corporation to administrative dissolution under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the fiscal period end (e.g., June 30 for a December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; additional penalties may apply for repeated failures or gross negligence. Registry strike-off does not apply to CRA tax filings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same due date as the federal T2 return; Alberta corporate tax is assessed on the federal T2 filing through the Alberta corporate tax allocation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Provincial corporate income tax arrears accrue interest and penalties administered by the CRA; enforced via CRA collection rather than Alberta registry dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For annual filers, no later than three months after the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 5% of the amount owing plus 1% per month for up to 12 months on late filers, plus arrears interest under the Excise Tax Act. CRA may set off refunds and impose director liability for unremitted trust amounts.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandatory solely by revenue or asset size for a non-distributing Alberta ULC. A mandatory independent audit is triggered if the corporation is a reporting issuer, becomes a distributing corporation, is a financial intermediary requiring statutory audit, or if a shareholder holding at least 5% of the voting shares applies to the court and an auditor is appointed. Otherwise, the shareholders may resolve unanimously to waive the appointment of an auditor under Alberta corporate law.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; Canadian ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for private, non-distributing corporations; IFRS may also be elected for private enterprises.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: An Alberta ULC must maintain an internal register of individuals with significant control (ISC). Annual confirmation is embedded in the Alberta Annual Return, which requires confirmation that the recorded shareholders, directors, and registered office information remains accurate. Any share transfer or change in significant control must be recorded in the register within 15 days of the corporation having notice, and the register must be updated continuously throughout the year.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - 1,200 per year for Alberta registered office and corporate agent services (approx. CAD 400 - 1,600 per year).
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - 18,000 for a certified audit of a small to mid-sized 3D animation production corporation; often reducible to a notice-to-reader or review engagement if the unanimous shareholder waiver of auditor appointment is validly adopted.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined headline rate on active business income (15% federal Part I general rate + 8% Alberta general corporate rate); reduced combined rate of 11% (federal 9% + Alberta 2%) applies to the first CAD 500,000 of active business income only if the ULC qualifies as a Canadian-controlled private corporation, which is precluded where a non-resident parent controls the entity
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal Canadian Film or Video Production Tax Credit (CPTC) of 25% of certified Canadian labour for Canadian-content 3D animation; federal Production Services Tax Credit (PSTC) of 16% of qualifying Canadian labour for foreign-service VFX/animation; Alberta Film and Television Tax Credit (AFTC) of 30% refundable on eligible Alberta labour expenditure; federal SR&ED Investment Tax Credit at 35% refundable (CCPC) or 15% non-refundable (non-CCPC) for proprietary animation tooling; these credits can reduce the effective federal Part I rate to approximately 0% on qualifying production income before provincial tax
